newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maybank says may raise BLR soon.
newsitem.headline: Maybank says may raise BLR soon.

text.p: Malayan Banking Bhd's managing director Amirsham Abdul Aziz said on Tuesday the bank may raise its key base lending rate (BLR) soon if interbank rates do not ease from a recent spike.
"We think this (rise in interbank rates) could be a short-term phenomenon. We are looking at maybe holding it a week, not more than a week, to see whether it's going back to normal.
"Then we will decide whether we will raise or keep our BLR," he told reporters on the sidelines of an Islamic banking conference on Labuan island.
The rise in money market rates in the last few weeks due to a liquidity squeeze have caused a number of banks in Malaysia to boost their BLR for June.
At present, most Malaysian banks are quoting the BLR between 9.50 and 9.60 percent. Maybank's BLR is among the lowest at 9.10 percent.
But Maybank's base rate, the rate a bank charges to its best customers, has been held steady at 9.1 percent.

Amirsham said the recent rise in interbank rates may be a short-term reaction caused by the central bank's intervention in the foreign exchange market to ward off speculation against the ringgit in the wake of the baht crisis.
He said Malaysian interest rates were expected to remain largely steady for the rest of the year as the central bank keeps a tight lid on inflation.
"I believe the authorities will not want to see that the inflation rate gets out of control, so I believe that it (interest rate) will stay as what it is," Amirsham said.
The Statistics Department last week reported that Malaysia's year-on-year inflation for May stood at 2.5 percent, against an annual increase of 2.6 percent in April and 3.2 percent in March.
